stocks.headline: Fell 14.0% to 125.53, a new 52-week low, ending its longest weekly losing streak since 2008. Morning call (don't buy): right.
stocks.why: The business is not the problem. Sales grew 106% last quarter, the operating margin is 65%, forecasts rose 27% in 90 days, and it trades at 9x next year's profit. The problem is legal. California's attorney general subpoenaed the company and said Nvidia may have misled investors, and the former CEO will testify before the Senate about his China ties. That kind of risk does not show up in earnings, so cheapness alone is not a reason to buy. Nvidia leads the whole chip group, so every new headline here also hits AMD, TSM, ARM, MU, AVGO and SMCI.

long_term.reason: This agrees with the house view. The company is cheap and still growing fast, but the subpoena and the Senate hearing are open legal risks to the company itself, not just to its share price.

stocks.what_would_change_it: If the investigation finds misleading statements or brings new China export limits, the stance moves to Avoid. If it closes back above 145.71 after the testimony with no new charges, the stance moves to Add on dips.
stocks.action: Don't buy the after-hours bounce or Monday's open. Buy a first slice only after a daily close back above 145.71.

stocks.headline: Fell 13.2% to 424.39 after a short-seller report on China links and news that US-approved chip sales reached groups tied to China's military. Morning call (don't buy the open): right.
stocks.why: The numbers are strong. Profit per share is up 74%, sales are up 45% and speeding up, it has beaten forecasts five quarters running, and it trades at 28x next year's profit. The damage comes from the claim that its firmware turned up at a blacklisted Chinese company. That raises the risk of export curbs or a probe like Nvidia's, and AMD has not answered the claim yet. The stock now sits right on its 200-day average of 429.79. That is the line between a pullback inside an uptrend and a broken trend.

long_term.reason: This agrees with the house view. Growth and forecasts are excellent, but an unanswered China allegation in the middle of the Nvidia scandal is the kind of news that keeps growing before it goes away.

stocks.what_would_change_it: A clear public rebuttal from AMD and a close back above 429.79 make it a Buy. A government probe or new export ban makes it Avoid.
